newsitem.title: USA: Yeltsin health not affecting IMF program - Camdessus.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin health not affecting IMF program - Camdessus.

text.p: International Monetary Fund Managing Director Michel Camdessus said Thursday that the health problems of Russian President Boris Yeltsin had not affected distribution of IMF loans to that country.
In an interview with Reuters Financial Television, Camdessus also expressed satisfaction with the current levels of the world's major currencies.
"It (Yeltsin's health) does not affect at all our disbursements. I don't percieve any vacuum in the way our program with russia is being implemented..." Camdessus said.
"We have continued disbursing month after month our participation to it (the program) and we intend to continue."
Camdessus described Yeltsin as the "key man" in Russia and it was important for the country to have a president in good health.
But he said the IMF program with Russia did not require presidential measures. "What is needed is central bank and government ready to continue to implement their pledges and they are doing that."

Camdessus expressed satisfaction with the relative strength of the world's major currencies when asked if it was desirable for the dollar to continue appreciating against the German mark to help ease pressure associated with European monetary union.
"The key currencies are now in, let's say, a solid, well-justified, constellation and we don't forsee major changes in the near future," he said.
"It (the dollar) is at the level where we cannot see its level as preventing all countries to grow more or less at their normal pace in a sustainable way."
Camdessus added that he felt Europe's efforts toward reforming their economies were "consolidating the prospects for the Euro to be one of the best currencies in the world."
